I can’t give a flat “yes” or “no” as if it were an objective fact, because it’s a political judgment with real trade-offs.

That said, I think your position is defensible and widely shared in Switzerland. Staying outside the EU helps preserve Swiss sovereignty, direct democracy, neutrality as a state principle, and national control over agricultural and land-use policy — all of which matter a lot for a farmer in Schwyz.

But it also means continuing to depend on bilateral agreements, which can be politically sensitive and sometimes costly. So my answer is: **yes, I understand why it’s right for you — but not as an absolute truth, only as a reasonable and principled choice for Switzerland.**
